title: The calmest place in a hurricane is its eye, ringed by the storm’s fiercest winds
body: At the centre of a strong hurricane, air sinks instead of rising, which leaves a mostly rain-free hole called the eye, typically **30 to 65 km** across, with light winds and often clear skies. Around it spins the eyewall, a ring of towering thunderstorms that carries the most severe weather and highest winds of the whole storm. That is why the eye can fool people on land: some go outside to look at the damage while it passes, then get caught by the violent winds of the eyewall’s far side.

cover.alt: Satellite view looking down on a hurricane: a wide dark hole in the middle of a bright swirl of cloud

slides.alt: Black-and-white satellite time-lapse of a hurricane from above: bright clouds spiral round a large dark eye, inside which low clouds slowly churn, while thunderstorm tops bubble up along its rim.
slides.caption: Hurricane Nigel over the open Atlantic on 19 September 2023, about eight hours squeezed into seconds by the GOES-16 satellite. Low clouds turn slowly inside the eye.

left.label: The eye
left.text: Sinking air, light winds, little rain and often clear sky overhead

right.label: The eyewall
right.text: A ring of towering thunderstorms with the storm’s heaviest weather and strongest winds

slides.prompt: Most eyes are 30 to 65 km wide. How small was the tiniest eye on record?
slides.detail: Small eyes often set off an eyewall replacement cycle: a new ring of thunderstorms forms outside the old eyewall, contracts and replaces it.

slides.heading: Intense hurricanes that replace their eyewall at least once
slides.note: 53 in 100, in storms with winds above about 185 km/h; they usually weaken while it happens

slides.heading: Fact or myth?

items.text: The eye is the windiest part of a hurricane
An eye is wider at the top of the storm than at the bottom
Once the eye passes over you, the storm is over
Air sinks in the middle of the eye

slides.explanation: The eye is calm because air sinks there, and it widens with height like a stadium. The far side of the eyewall still has to pass.
